h1: The 6 Best Patio Heaters of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 patio heaters scored on BTU or wattage, coverage claims, tip-over safety and base design, from propane towers to infrared.
summary: The Sweetcrispy 48,000 BTU propane heater is the best all-round patio heater here, with a built-in side table and both flame-out and tilt shutoffs. The Hykolity 50,000 BTU with a weight-adjustable base is the choice for windy decks. The Amazon Basics 46,000 BTU is the plain, trusted-brand tower, and the three electric infrared models suit covered patios.
intro: Patio heater shopping starts with a mistake: comparing BTU numbers across propane and electric models as if they were the same thing. A propane tower heats by radiating and convecting in open air, while a 1500W infrared panel warms whatever it points at within a few feet. Same word, different jobs.

Six heaters made this ranking, three propane towers, a pyramid tower and two infrared electrics, ordered by fit rather than raw output. We weighed listed heat output, stated coverage, base stability, safety shutoffs and fuel or power practicality. Coverage claims are marketing numbers, so we trust them less than the shutoff features and base design, which are the parts you can verify.

products.name: Sweetcrispy 48,000 BTU Propane Patio Heater
products.verdict: A table-equipped propane tower with flame-out and tilt shutoffs.
products.description:
Sweetcrispy's tower puts out 48,000 BTU through a double-layer 304 stainless burner and includes a round side table. It claims an 18-foot diameter for 4 to 8 people, with a flame-out cutoff and a 45 degree tilt sensor. It costs $100 to $200.

The round table makes it more than a heater: you can set a drink on it without carrying a side stand. The two safety cutoffs are what put it first, since flame-out and tilt are the failure modes that matter outdoors. It beats the Hykolity 50,000 BTU on documented safety, though the Hykolity has the more stable base. Treat the 18-foot claim as a ceiling, not a typical result.

Buy it for a patio seating four to six. Plan on propane tank storage and refills as ongoing costs.
products.idealFor: Patios seating four to six people.
products.skipIf: You want an electric heater with no propane.

products.name: Hykolity 50,000 BTU Patio Heater With Sand Box Table
products.verdict: 50,000 BTU on a weight-adjustable conical base for stability.
products.description:
Hykolity's heater is rated at 50,000 BTU, uses a double-layer 304 stainless steel burner and sits on a conical, weight-adjustable base with a sand box table. The listing states it heats up to 200 square feet. It costs $100 to $200.

The weight-adjustable base is the headline. Tower heaters tip in gusts, and a base you can fill to your liking is the most direct fix. It is the highest-rated in BTU, yet ranks second because the listing documents fewer safety features than the Sweetcrispy. The 200 square foot figure is the most modest and believable coverage claim in the group.

Buy it for an open deck or a breezy yard. Skip it if you move the heater often, since a filled base is heavy.

products.name: Amazon Basics 46,000 BTU Portable Propane Patio Heater
products.verdict: 46,000 BTU with a water tank base, tilt shutoff and tank chain.
products.description:
This tower produces 46,000 BTU with a stated 9-foot radius, a water-tank base for weight, a tilt auto-shutoff valve and a tank chain. It costs $100 to $200.

A water tank base is less common than sand or a concrete block. You fill it on site, and it drains for storage, so the heater is light to move. The tank chain secures the propane cylinder against knocks. It ranks third because 46,000 BTU is lower than the two above, and the 9-foot radius claim is no better than the others. Compared with the Sweetcrispy, you do not get a table.

Buy it if you want a straightforward tower with a known brand. Water bases can freeze in winter, so drain it before a cold snap.
cons: Lower BTU than the top two
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a simple, portable tower.

products.name: Hykolity 48,000 BTU Pyramid Patio Heater With Cover
products.verdict: A 90 inch glass-tube pyramid with a cover and 8 to 10 hours per tank.
products.description:
This pyramid heater delivers 48,000 BTU from a 90 inch tall glass-tube pyramid and ships with a cover. The listing states 8 to 10 hours per 20 lb propane tank and a 45 degree anti-tilt shutoff. It costs $200 to $500, the highest bucket here.

The glass tube gives a flame view that a plain tower lacks, which is why people choose pyramids for a restaurant look. The documented runtime is the best in the ranking, because no other listing gives hours per tank. It ranks fourth because you pay up to $500 for essentially the same BTU as the Sweetcrispy. The included cover is a practical extra for winter storage.

Buy it for visual impact and a documented runtime. Skip it on a tight budget or a low-ceiling patio.
products.idealFor: Patios where the heater is part of the look.
products.skipIf: You have a low roof or a tight budget.

products.name: Hykolity 1500W Electric Infrared Patio Heater, 38.5 Inch
products.verdict: 1500W infrared with a 0 to 24 hour timer and tip-over protection.
products.description:
This electric infrared heater is 1500W with two heat levels, a 0 to 24 hour timer, IP44 and ETL certification, and tip-over and overheat shutoffs. It stands 38.5 inches tall and costs $100 to $200.

Infrared warms people directly instead of the air, which is why it works under a covered patio and not in open wind. The timer and two heat levels are conveniences the propane towers lack. It ranks fifth because 1500W does not match a propane tower's reach, and IP44 handles splashes, not a soaking. It suits a small seating spot, not a party.

Buy it for a covered porch with an outlet and a single chair or two. Skip it for open decks and larger groups.
products.idealFor: Covered porches and small seating spots.
products.skipIf: You heat open decks or large groups.

products.name: DR. INFRARED Portable Infrared Patio Heater 1500W
products.verdict: Three power levels, IP55 and freestanding, wall or ceiling mounting.
products.description:
The DR. INFRARED heater offers 900W, 1200W and 1500W settings, an IP55 rating, a remote and wall and ceiling brackets alongside freestanding use. It runs on 120V at 60Hz and has no thermostat. It costs $100 to $200.

Three wattage steps give finer control than the two-level Hykolity, and IP55 handles water jets better than IP44. Wall or ceiling mounting is the standout, since an overhead infrared panel does not take floor space. It ranks last because no thermostat means it never cycles itself, and 1500W is still an infrared supplement, not a patio furnace.

Buy it for a covered area where you can mount it above a seating group. Skip it if you want automatic temperature control.
products.idealFor: Covered patios with an overhead mount spot.

whatMatters.detail: Propane towers are rated in BTU, such as 48,000, and electric infrared in watts, such as 1500W. They are not directly comparable, because infrared warms objects while propane heats air. Match the type to the space: towers for open patios, infrared for covered, enclosed spots. Check the listing's stated units.

Listed coverage, like 18 feet diameter or 200 square feet, is a best-case figure in still air. Wind and cold cut it sharply. The Hykolity 50,000 BTU's 200 square feet is modest and credible. Treat larger claims as ceilings, and place seats within a few feet of the heater.

A flame-out cutoff shuts the gas if the flame dies, and a tilt sensor closes it if the heater falls. The Sweetcrispy lists both. Look for named shutoffs and certifications on the listing, and never use a propane heater under a low roof or in an enclosed area.

A tower heater tips in gusts, so the base matters. The Hykolity uses a weight-adjustable conical base, the Amazon Basics a water tank. Check how the base is filled, how heavy it is when full and whether it can be drained for storage.

Propane towers need tank refills, and a 20 lb tank runs 8 to 10 hours on the Hykolity pyramid. Electric models need an outlet and run indefinitely. Check whether tanks fit inside the base, how the cylinder is secured and whether a cover is included.

faq.q: Can I use a propane patio heater under a covered porch?
faq.a: Not unless the manual says so. Propane towers like the Sweetcrispy and Amazon Basics need open air and clearance. For covered spaces, choose electric infrared such as the Hykolity 1500W or the DR. INFRARED, and keep clear of combustibles.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with patio heaters?
faq.a: Believing the coverage claim. The Sweetcrispy says 18 feet, but wind and cold shrink that sharply. Seat people within a few feet of the heater, and read the Hykolity 50,000 BTU's 200 square feet as the realistic reference.

faq.q: Is the Hykolity Pyramid worth it over the Sweetcrispy?
faq.a: Only for the looks and the cover. Both are around 48,000 BTU, the Pyramid lists 8 to 10 hours per tank, and costs up to $500. The Sweetcrispy adds a table at $100 to $200.

faq.q: How do I set up the Amazon Basics base?
faq.a: Fill the water tank base before attaching the propane cylinder, then use the tank chain to secure it. The base drains for storage, so empty it before freezing weather to avoid cracks.

faq.q: How do I maintain a propane heater?
faq.a: Cover it when idle, as the Hykolity Pyramid includes, check hose and connections for leaks with soapy water, and keep the burner clear of spiders and debris. Store the tank upright outdoors.

faq.q: Do the electric models need special wiring?
faq.a: The DR. INFRARED runs on 120V at 60Hz and the Hykolity on a standard plug, so a normal outlet works. Use an outdoor-rated cord, and keep the plug off wet ground.

finalTake: The Sweetcrispy 48,000 BTU is the best patio heater for most open patios, thanks to its flame-out and tilt shutoffs and built-in table. The Hykolity 50,000 BTU wins on a breezy deck because of its weight-adjustable base. For covered porches, choose the Hykolity 1500W with its timer or the DR. INFRARED for overhead mounting.
